newsitem.title: USA: US 2-yr T-note yield dips below 6 pct on May PPI.
newsitem.headline: US 2-yr T-note yield dips below 6 pct on May PPI.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury two-year note yield dipped below six percent at mid-morning on Friday as the market extended its advance on an even more favorable than expected May wholesale price report.

Shortly after 1020 EDT/1400 GMT, the U.S. Treasury two-year note was priced at 100-15/32, yielding 5.991 percent, its lowest yield since the close on February 25, the eve of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's last Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

Earlier in the trading session, the government reported that the U.S. Producer Price Index fell 0.3 percent in May after dropping 0.6 percent in April. The core PPI, the index without its more volatile food and energy components, also dropped 0.3 percent after slipping 0.1 percent in April.
Economists had expected the overall and the core PPI each to rise a modest 0.1 percent.
In mid-morning trade, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 23/32 to 98-25/32, yielding 6.72 percent. In the equity market, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 66 points.
Financial markets rallied on Thursday after the government reported more subdued than expected retail sales for May.

"Now the second shoe drops with amazingly good price statistics," said David Jones, vice chairman and economist at Aubrey G. Lanston. "(For) the financial markets, it just doesn't get any better than this."
